cards.title: Constraints as Creative Catalysts
cards.insight: The most innovative solutions often emerge from tight limitations rather than unlimited resources. A narrow budget, strict timeline, or technical constraint forces fresh thinking and unexpected problem-solving paths that abundance might obscure.
cards.takeaway: When facing a project bottleneck, reframe it as a creative boundary rather than a barrier—identify one limitation and ask 'what becomes possible within this constraint?'

cards.title: Cross-Domain Inspiration Mining
cards.insight: Breakthrough ideas rarely come from deep specialization alone. Combining concepts from unrelated fields—biology applied to engineering, music patterns applied to data visualization—creates novel connections your competitors haven't made.
cards.takeaway: Spend 30 minutes weekly exploring an industry or discipline completely outside your expertise and note one unexpected principle you could adapt to your work.

cards.title: Failure as Feedback Loop
cards.insight: Creative work requires rapid iteration; failed experiments generate more learning than endless planning. Each misstep reveals what doesn't work and points toward what might, creating momentum that analysis alone cannot.
cards.takeaway: Set a weekly target for 'creative failures'—launch three half-baked ideas and document what each one teaches about your actual problem.

cards.title: Incubation Over Intensity
cards.insight: Sustained creative breakthroughs emerge from alternating between focused work and genuine rest, not marathon grinding sessions. The subconscious continues pattern-matching during breaks, surfacing solutions conscious effort missed.
cards.takeaway: Schedule 'walk breaks' during complex creative work—step away for 15 minutes every 90 minutes and notice how problems often clarify in the silence.
